PDF data extraction for spreadsheet entr: Use openpyxl/pandas to read the result xlsx and compare specific cell values (numeric) with approx tolerance via check_cell rules; the compare_table metric supports 'approx:N' method for floating-point amounts extracted from PDFs.

When verifying transaction amounts parsed from PDF receipts/invoices, use sheet_fuzzy exact_match for text fields (category, description) and check_cell approx match for numeric fields (amounts, running balances).

Running balance/cumulative columns can be verified by checking each row's cell value independently with approx tolerance rather than comparing full column ranges, since small extraction errors compound.

PDF text extraction tools (pdfplumber, PyMuPDF, pdfminer) vary in how they parse tables vs. free-form text; verify that currency symbols, negative signs, and decimal separators are correctly parsed before numeric comparison.
Use fitz (PyMuPDF) to extract text from each page via page.get_text() and compare with fuzz.ratio for fuzzy text similarity scoring
PDF file organization/copying into folde: Verify the correct PDF ends up at the target path by extracting and fuzzy-comparing its text content against a reference PDF; fitz.open + page.get_text() is the standard extraction approach, and fuzz.ratio >= threshold indicates a match
PDF form filling from spreadsheet data: Use PyMuPDF (fitz) to extract text from each page and compare against reference PDFs using fuzzy string matching (e.g., fuzz.ratio) averaged across multiple files.
When verifying checkbox/mark fields, extract raw text and check for presence of the specific mark character (e.g., √) in the correct positions relative to surrounding label text.
For multi-file batch output, iterate over all expected output files and average similarity scores; a missing file should contribute 0 to the score.
PDF text extraction via fitz page.get_text() captures both static text and filled form field values as a flat string, making fuzz.ratio a practical similarity metric for form content comparison.
PDF file naming based on data field valu: Check that output filenames exactly match the employee/entity name strings as they appear in the source data, including spaces and capitalization.
Use os.path.exists or directory listing to verify each expected filename is present before attempting content comparison.
PDF author identification: Author order (first, last N) must be extracted from PDF metadata or rendered text; use PDF parsing libraries to read author lists from title pages or headers.

Verification relies on cross-referencing extracted author names against expected personal webpage URLs, so the checker must tolerate multiple valid URL aliases per author (use itertools.product over per-author URL sets and compare as sets).
Image to PDF conversion: Use fitz (PyMuPDF) to extract embedded images from each PDF page via page.get_images() and pdf_document.extract_image(); compare extracted images between result and reference using perceptual hashing (e.g., imagehash.phash) with a small hash-difference threshold to tolerate minor encoding differences
Check that the number of embedded images across all pages matches between result and reference PDF before doing content comparison
When a PDF is created by embedding an image, the image may be re-encoded (JPEG, PNG, etc.); perceptual hash comparison is more robust than pixel-exact or byte-exact comparison for this feature class
merged PDF page order verification: For image-based or scanned PDFs, text extraction may be empty; evaluators should not fall back to page count only. Render pages or compare page/image fingerprints to verify the exact source page order.

For PDF Arranger merge tasks, do not rely only on PyPDF2 extract_text snippets for page identity, especially with scanned or image-heavy PDFs; use rendered page hashes or stronger content/resource fingerprints to distinguish pages and verify ordering.
PDF merge order verification: For merged PDF order checks, low-resolution perceptual hashes can be too weak for similar text/scanned pages; use stronger deterministic page comparison such as extracted text plus higher-resolution normalized pixmap differences or exact rendered-page hashes.
merged PDF page-order verification: For stricter merged-PDF verification, compare rendered source and result pages with high thresholds and an off-diagonal margin or use deterministic page fingerprints; low-resolution mean pixel similarity can over-reward blank or visually similar pages and should avoid treating ties as correct matches.

For merged PDFs, avoid dimension-only or text-only partial scoring because scanned/image PDFs may have empty extracted text and identical page dimensions; combine an exact page-count check with rendered-page or source-page identity checks in the required order.

For PDF Arranger merge tasks, text overlap is useful but a stronger evaluator should compare each output page to the corresponding source page using rendered-page hashes or PDF page text plus dimensions to reduce false positives from manually recreated text.
merged PDF verification: A PDF evaluator must return 0 for missing or unreadable output files; do not treat all exceptions as optional dependency failures or award fallback credit, because this causes positive initial-state reward.
merged PDF order verification: For merged PDFs, compare rendered pages against every page of each source PDF in the expected sequence, or first confirm source page counts, rather than assuming each input PDF is single-page.

For PDF Arranger merge tasks, do not rely on total page count plus one loose first/last text anchor. Build an expected ordered page sequence from the source PDFs and compare each merged page using extracted text hashes and/or rendered page fingerprints to prove ordering and inclusion.

For PDF Arranger merge tasks, verifying the rendered page hash sequence of the output against the source PDFs is a strong order check, but prefer dependencies known to be available or include a fallback such as PyPDF2 page count/text/object checks.
rotated PDF verification: A rotated PDF rule should verify both page rotation metadata and extracted page text/content, otherwise an unrelated blank one-page PDF with /Rotate=90 can falsely pass.
A rotated-PDF evaluator should combine exact page count, /Rotate value, and required document text/content matching; rotation alone is too easy to satisfy with an unrelated PDF.
sender substring validation: Avoid using a broad sender substring that also appears in the subject or other required text, because it can make the sender check pass even when the sender is missing.
PDF page duplication verification: For duplicate-page tasks, checking only the output page count and equality of adjacent pages is not source-grounded; retrieve the original PDF and compare the expected output page sequence against the source pages.

For exported PDF page-order checks, text extraction plus word counts is useful but can miss layout/content differences; stronger evaluators should compare page dimensions and either rendered page image hashes or low-level page content/object fingerprints against the source pages.
duplicate PDF page verification: For PDF duplication tasks, text extraction alone is a weak verifier because visually or structurally different pages with the same text can pass; compare page objects/resources or rendered page hashes when the task requires duplicating exact pages.
plain-text exact-line audit files: When the instruction requires exactly one line, avoid using strip() on the whole line because it permits leading/trailing spaces and extra blank trailing lines; compare the raw content against the exact allowed string plus optionally a single final newline.
PDF output verification: When verifying a PDF saved in the VM, use a vm_file getter for the PDF and open the returned local cached path in rule code; do not directly access /home/user/Desktop/... from the rule judge.
PDF merge/reorder verification: For PDF Arranger reorder tasks, the strongest evaluator should parse the exported PDF and require exact page count plus exact per-page text order; avoid giving substantial independent credit for merely being a valid PDF or having the right number of pages.
PDF page-order verification: For PDF Arranger merge/reorder tasks, verify the exported PDF with an internal PDF parser for exact page count and ordered per-page text. If using pdfplumber in a vm_command_line getter, include a PyPDF2 fallback or avoid making correctness depend on a non-guaranteed parser.
PDF page deletion and rotation: For PDF Arranger tasks, robust verification should parse the saved PDF structure: check page count/order using extracted page text and check rotation metadata on the specific output page, preferably normalizing rotation modulo 360 and using common PDF libraries such as pypdf/PyPDF2.
PDF page order verification: For PDF merge/reorder tasks, avoid keyword-only checks; fetch or reference the source PDFs and compare each output page to the corresponding source page using extracted text, page count, or rendered-page hashes to prove the exact source files and order.
initial-state false positives: A rule that only validates sampled source files or expected data, without checking a user-created artifact, can produce positive initial reward and should be removed or converted into an expected_getter used by an artifact-checking rule.
